citation: Altman, E. I. (1968). Financial ratios, discriminant analysis and the prediction of corporate bankruptcy. Journal of Finance 23(4), 589-609
informs_decision: Seed. No claim is taken from it: the publisher page shows the citation only and the full text is paywalled. The Z-score enters this stream only as used by Asness et al. 2019 (a safety component) and as assessed by Campbell et al. 2008

citation: Beneish, M. D. (1999). The detection of earnings manipulation. Financial Analysts Journal 55(5), 24-36
feature: financial statement variables that capture distortions from manipulation or incentives to manipulate
method: probability-of-manipulation model on a profiled sample of manipulators; sample size not checked
informs_decision: Structured baseline for the Item 4.02 tier: the abstract reports that the model identifies about half of manipulators before public discovery. Checked at abstract level only

citation: Piotroski, J. D. (2000). Value investing: the use of historical financial statement information to separate winners from losers. Journal of Accounting Research 38 (Supplement), 1-41
feature: accounting-based signals of financial strength among high book-to-market firms
outcome: annual stock returns; earnings announcement reactions
informs_decision: Candidate definition of fundamental strength or deterioration for the softer tier: selecting financially strong high book-to-market firms raises the mean return by at least 7.5% a year and the long-short strategy earns 23% a year, concentrated in small and thinly followed firms. Abstract level only; delisting treatment not checked

citation: Campbell, J. Y., Hilscher, J., Szilagyi, J. (2008). In search of distress risk. Journal of Finance 63(6), 2899-2939; read as NBER WP 12362 (2006)
feature: eight accounting and market variables: profitability, leverage, past excess return, volatility, relative size, cash, market-to-book, price per share
method: dynamic logit on a monthly panel, 1963-2003; portfolios sorted on fitted failure probability, 1981-2003
outcome: bankruptcy filing; failure (bankruptcy, delisting or D rating); returns of failure-sorted portfolios
incremental_to: Shumway (2001) five-variable model; Merton distance to default
pit_handling: accounting data lagged two months; out-of-sample coefficients re-estimated yearly from 1981; Compustat vintage not addressed
informs_decision: Failure definition; base rates (bankruptcy 0.36-1.53% of CRSP firms a year in 1980-1998, failure 1.52-3.67% in 1998-2003); the structured baseline a text signal must beat (pseudo-R2 0.31 at one month, 0.11 at twelve); delisting returns matter

citation: Mayew, W. J., Sethuraman, M., Venkatachalam, M. (2015). MD&A disclosure and the firm's ability to continue as a going concern. The Accounting Review 90(4), 1621-1651
feature: management going-concern statement; negative and positive word use
method: matched-pair conditional logit; firms filing for bankruptcy 1995-2012
incremental_to: financial ratios, market-based variables, auditor going-concern opinion
pit_handling: not addressed in the abstract or the authors' summary; matched-pair AUC, no out-of-sample test reported there
informs_decision: Closest precedent for narrative against fundamentals. Authors' 2013 summary of the working paper: MD&A-only AUC 0.85 against 0.90 for ratios one year ahead and 0.73 against 0.66 three years ahead; 0.91 combined; managers mention going-concern doubt in 38% of later bankruptcies and auditors in 43.5%. Full text not opened; sample counts unverified

citation: Brown, N. C., Crowley, R. M., Elliott, W. B. (2020). What are you saying? Using topic to detect financial misreporting. Journal of Accounting Research 58(1), 237-291
feature: topic proportions from a Bayesian topic model
method: topic model plus out-of-sample detection tests
outcome: misreporting: SEC enforcement releases (AAERs); irregularities from restatements and 10-K amendments
incremental_to: financial variables and textual style variables
pit_handling: out-of-sample tests stated in the abstract; detail not checked
informs_decision: Text baseline for the Item 4.02 tier: topics improve detection by up to 59% over models using financial and style variables. Abstract level only; full text paywalled

citation: Asness, C. S., Frazzini, A., Pedersen, L. H. (2019). Quality minus junk. Review of Accounting Studies 24(1), 34-112
feature: quality score: profitability, growth, safety (safety includes O-score and Z-score)
method: portfolio sorts and factor regressions; US 1957-2016, 24 countries 1989-2016
outcome: price-to-book; returns of the quality-minus-junk factor
incremental_to: market, size, value and momentum factors
pit_handling: accounting data used from June of the following year; Compustat vintage not addressed
informs_decision: Definition of fundamental quality for the softer tier; junk rallies (QMJ market loading -0.20, raw return zero in months when volatility falls sharply); missing performance-related delisting returns set to -30%

citation: Shumway, T. (1997). The delisting bias in CRSP data. Journal of Finance 52(1), 327-340 (companion checked at abstract level: Shumway and Warther 1999, Journal of Finance 54(6), 2361-2379)
method: over-the-counter prices used to estimate the omitted delisting returns
informs_decision: Supports the default that return studies must include delisted stocks: delistings for negative reasons are generally surprises, most lack a correct delisting return, and the omitted returns are large (abstract). Magnitudes were not checked in the paper itself: -30% is the convention Asness et al. 2019 attribute to it, and -55% for Nasdaq is from the Shumway-Warther abstract (https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:bla:jfinan:v:54:y:1999:i:6:p:2361-2379). Full text paywalled

citation: Lerman, A., Livnat, J. (2010). The new Form 8-K disclosures. Review of Accounting Studies 15(4), 752-778; read as SSRN working paper, draft of 29 April 2008
text_source: 8-K item codes and dates (no text analysis); 10-K and 10-Q filing dates
outcome: abnormal return, volume and volatility; drift after filing
horizon: 3 days around event and filing; 30 to 90 days after
incremental_to: size and book-to-market matched portfolio returns
pit_handling: separates event date from EDGAR filing date; point-in-time Compustat link that keeps inactive firms
informs_decision: Hard-event tier: counts and price reactions for Items 1.03, 2.06, 3.01 and 4.02 (18, 532, 2,137 and 1,124 filings in two years); about 95% of filings arrive within four business days

citation: Dechow, P. M., Ge, W., Larson, C. R., Sloan, R. G. (2011). Predicting material accounting misstatements. Contemporary Accounting Research 28(1), 17-82
text_source: none (enforcement releases read by hand to build labels)
feature: F-score from financial statement variables, including accrual quality, soft assets, change in cash sales, change in return on assets and security issuance
method: logit on misstatement firm-years from 2,190 AAERs, 1982-2005; holdout 1999-2002 and rolling-window tests
outcome: earnings overstatement alleged in an SEC enforcement release
pit_handling: holdout and rolling-window tests reported; timing of labels relative to detection not checked
informs_decision: Base rate and structured baseline for misreporting: 0.37% of firm-years (494 of 133,461); at an F-score cutoff of 1.00 sensitivity is 68.6% and the false-positive rate 36.3%; 676 misstating firms. Full text read in part; no deep note

citation: Doidge, C., Karolyi, G. A., Stulz, R. M. (2017). The U.S. listing gap. Journal of Financial Economics 123(3), 464-487; read as NBER WP 21181 (2015); update to 2023 read in Doidge, Karolyi, Shen and Stulz (2025), NBER WP 33556
feature: CRSP delisting codes: 200-399 merger; 400 and above for cause, except 570 and 573 (voluntary)
method: counts and rates of new lists and delists among US exchange-listed firms, 1975-2012; update to 2023
informs_decision: Base rate and working definition of delisting for cause: 7,120 for-cause delists in 1975-2012; 3.25% of listed firms a year in 1975-1996 and 3.50% in 1997-2012; the update reports the rate as extremely low in 2014-2021 and sharply higher in 2022-2023 (figure only, no numbers in the text)

citation: Zhang, Z., Zheng, M., Zhang, T., Lin, L., Wang, Y., Lin, L. (2026). Bankruptcy prediction from 10-K narratives: evidence from interpretable text scores and accounting baselines. arXiv:2606.05623
feature: dictionary-based Pre-Bankruptcy Stress score in five pillars
method: classification with a fixed 80/20 holdout and out-of-time checks; 40,475 firm-years, 128 bankruptcies from the Florida-UCLA-LoPucki database
outcome: bankruptcy filing within 365 days of the 10-K filing date
incremental_to: five accounting ratios; Loughran-McDonald negative and uncertainty words
pit_handling: predictors and text limited to what was available at the filing date; no language model used
informs_decision: Recent bar for text against ratios in distress prediction: holdout AUC rises from 0.832 to 0.902 (difference 0.070, bootstrap interval 0.035 to 0.111) on 34 events; base rate 0.32% of firm-years. Preprint, not peer reviewed; checked on the arXiv HTML version; may belong mainly to stream 01
